messages:
emma (partnerships): quick heads-up, customer tried to buy via AWS Marketplace but hit a procurement blocker — their procurement says they can only issue a PO to the "Vendor" name listed in Marketplace and our onboarding isn't complete. also they flagged a few contract redlines (data residency + payment term). who can help escalate?
rafael (sales): ah, which customer and what's the payment term they're asking for? net30/net45?
emma (partnerships): Acme Bio. they want net45, and they asked for an explicit Data Processing Addendum in the contract; they also want vendor name on the PO to match AWS listing (they won't accept a direct invoice).
maria (legal): can we get the exact redline text? usually DPA + standard security appendix is fine. what is the risk ask on liability/indemnity?
emma (partnerships): pasted from their PO email: "We require the Vendor to include an addendum detailing data residency in EU and processor obligations. Payment terms: Net45. PO will be issued to the registered marketplace vendor only."
aya (solutions): workaround question — can we route them to Dedicated/Private and do a direct SOW+invoice? customer insists on marketplace because of internal procurement rules.
kevin (finance): for marketplace PO flows we still need vendor onboarding in AWS to get the PO routed to our finance entity. that onboarding can take 2-5 business days unless we already have a marketplace listing. do we have an active AWS seller account for the product SKU?
emma (partnerships): not yet. Partnerships is fast-tracking marketplace listing but it's pending legal & finance signoffs. asking if we can accept the PO outside marketplace and then reconcile — but buyer says it's policy to use marketplace line items.
maria (legal): redlines: they're asking to remove our liability cap and add an audit clause. we should push back on removing cap; propose limiting audits to 1/year with SOC reports accepted. for DPA: we can attach our standard DPA with EU SCCs.
rafael (sales): customer is firm; procurement said no exceptions. maybe we can ask Marketplace to add our vendor name temporarily to allow PO? any contacts at AWS?
emma (partnerships): tagging @aws-seller-support-bot to open a support case for expedited vendor onboarding. can Partnerships own that request and cc finance + legal? :eyes:
aws-seller-support-bot: Case created: #MC-75632. ETA initial response 24h. Please provide company legal name, vendor tax id, and marketplace product SKU.
kevin (finance): I'll get vendor tax id & W9 ready. finance won't approve vendor onboarding without the W9 and bank details.
maria (legal): I'll draft a slim addendum: include DPA w/ SCCs, keep liability cap, limit audits. sending draft in thread in ~2h.
aya (solutions): also flag to customer success to hold the integration work until we confirm procurement flow. don't want them to start work if PO won't come through.
emma (partnerships): plan: 1) Partnerships to submit expedited seller onboarding (aws case). 2) Finance provides W9 + vendor info. 3) Legal provides DPA/limited audit language. 4) Sales asks customer procurement to accept marketplace PO once vendor registered. target: unblock in 48-72h.
rafael (sales): ok will update the buyer and set expectation for ~72h.
kevin (finance): finance will prioritise W9 today.
maria (legal): draft sent — see snippet below for review by Partnerships/Finance:
```
Minimal Addendum: Vendor will process EU customer data per SCCs. Audit requests limited to 1 per year; SOC2 accepted. Liability cap remains at direct damages up to contract value. No unlimited indemnity.
```
emma (partnerships): thanks all. I'll follow up on the AWS case and post updates. filing internal playbook note so we don't hit same blocker again. :thumbsup:
rafael (sales): appreciate it — cc'ing customer contact to keep momentum.
aya (solutions): marked as blocked in Jira: PROJ-412 marketplace-po-wait.
emma (partnerships): closing note: if AWS seller support can add vendor name to PO routing quickly, we should be able to accept customer's marketplace PO without changing payment terms. otherwise fall back to direct invoice but that will require procurement exception.
